label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Subject: Re: Our plan for next year

Dear all,

Sorry for the slow reply, I've just come off a run of nights and only properly sat down with everything today.

First, Appa and Amma, I'm so happy you're coming. I keep thinking about it on the drive home. The children are beside themselves. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable for the fridge, and one of the entries is "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays." I've been told it is not negotiable.

Kiran, you're right, and I'm sorry. I should have told you much earlier, and that's on me. It honestly started in August, when Rohan was showing Appa the vegetable patch on video and Appa said, "I could grow drumsticks there." We got talking from there. Then the visa agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, so I started gathering paperwork, and that was the point where I should have rung you and Divya. I didn't, and you ended up hearing it as an announcement. I'd have felt the same. Thank you for putting your concerns down plainly. They're the right questions and I'd rather we talk them through properly.

1. Appa's heart

This is the one I've thought about most, and you're correct that visitors aren't covered for free NHS treatment. So this is what I've arranged:

- Insurance: I have a travel insurance quote that includes pre-existing cardiac cover, about £640 each for the six months. The agent has confirmed it covers the stent. Before we buy it I'll get that confirmation in writing and send the policy wording round so anyone can read it.
- Dr. Prakash: He has agreed to do Appa's full review in March before they fly, and a video consult in July while they're here. He's happy to share his notes with me, so his care carries on the whole time. If the March review says anything that worries him, we change the plan. That decision is his, not mine.
- If something did happen: Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from the house, and I know a lot of the cardiology team there. Appa would be seen quickly and by people I trust.
- The house: the annexe at the back is finished. It's on the ground floor with no steps, and it has its own shower with a grab rail.

I won't pretend there's no risk at all, because there's a risk anywhere. But I wouldn't be comfortable with this if I didn't think he'd be safe and well looked after.

2. Amma and six months

That's fair, and it isn't something I'd thought about enough. Amma, six months is the maximum the visa allows, not a commitment. The return ticket is flexible. If at six weeks or three months you miss home, your own kitchen, your friends, you go back, and nobody will think anything of it. I'd much rather you came and left early than felt stuck here.

3. Ganesh Chaturthi

I don't want this to cost Pune anything. Two options I can see:

- Amma and Appa fly from Leicester to Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi in September and finish the trip with you, then head home to Bangalore from there.
- Or all of you come here in August, and I'd like to cover your flights for that. Please let me. Anika and Rohan would love having their cousins here, and Appa can show off his drumsticks.

We could even do both. Whatever works best for you.

I think the easiest thing is to talk properly instead of over email. Could we do a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? Appa and Amma, Divya and Kiran and the Pune lot, all of us. Kiran, if you have more worries I haven't answered, I'd really like to hear them, and if we need to change parts of this plan, we will. Nothing is submitted until January.

Divya, the murukku achu is noted. Amma, consider it officially requested.

Love to everyone,
Meera
